title: research-agent-tests: an audit of agent instruction files in research software and a 5-bug pilot on agent-written regression tests
description:
Evidence for one question: when a coding agent fixes a bug in research software and also writes the regression test, does the test prove anything, or does it share the fix's misunderstanding?

audit/: 38 widely used research software repositories checked for root-level agent instruction files (20 have one); all 20 files read in full and tabulated by what they say about tests.

pilot/: 5 real wrong-result bugs (networkx, pint, xarray, mne-python) and 18 agent runs. In round 2 the agent wrote both the fix and the test: 9 of 9 reported that their test failed before the fix and passed after, 2 of 9 fixes were wrong, and the agent's own test passed on the wrong fix. Grading is mechanical. Scripts, prompts, agent-written tests, diffs, verdicts and token use are included.

These are pilot numbers for a larger study design, not results. See README.md for how to reproduce and for the limits.
